Grammar error suites for scripts/accuracy-benchmark.mjs.

Each suite maps an error category to [error, corrected] sentence pairs. Each
error sentence holds one planted error, and its corrected twin differs only
where the fix requires. A finding on the error sentence that the twin lacks
counts as a catch; any grammar finding on the twin counts as a false alarm.
The sentences read like software documentation a person wrote with an AI
assistant and then edited by hand.

- dev-suite.json: 172 pairs in 33 categories, written 2026-09-26 while the
  native patterns were designed. The patterns were tuned against it, so its
  score overstates recall.
- heldout-suite.json: 180 pairs in 30 categories, written 2026-09-26 by a
  fresh Claude Sonnet session with no access to Terse's code or patterns.
  Its score is the recall estimate. One false alarm on a corrected twin led
  to a precision fix after the recall figure was recorded.
- clause-suite.json: agreement across a phrase, comma splices, and run-ons,
  each with 25 [error, corrected] pairs and 25 correct lookalikes built to
  trip a naive checker. Written 2026-09-26 by a fresh Claude Sonnet session
  with no access to Terse, and scored once before any tuning: 4, 9, and 0
  of 25 caught, no lookalike flagged. The one false alarm on a corrected
  sentence led to a precision fix in the AnA rule afterwards.
